output.name: Nelu
output.myth: When Ennu the Kite-Wright was still green, he built a red kite to carry a bargain over rough water. The boats of the north and the boats of the south could not row to meet. So he sewed a salt token into the belly of the kite, tied its string to one boat's stern, and let it run over the white sea. Tavo the Gale came laughing from the south-west, past the Upturned Hull lying keel-up on the swell, and tore the cloth at the top. The string held. Up in the north, the Sun-Kite's Ribbon streamed loose and watched it all from above. The token dropped into the second boat's hands, and the old women on shore took in their long-tail kites. The bargain was made. Tavo is still sore he was not asked. Hesk counted the string, out and back, and found it true. So when two boats under the Leeward Reach agree on a price without shouting, the old ones say the Nelu is flying tonight, and a fair trade is a kite that comes home.
output.finding: Find Tirun, the Upturned Hull, low in the south-west, then look a little over half a hand-span to its north-east for Nelu.
